orchard/api-versioning.md.text:
# API versioning policy

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-09-10.

The current scheme is **CalVer** (`YYYY.MM.PATCH`). Adopted 2026-07-01.

Historical note: the vault used **SemVer** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) until
2026-06-30. SemVer references in older pages are superseded by this document.

Breaking changes require a deprecation window of 90 days.

orchard/data-retention.md.text:
# Data retention policy

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-07-20.

Draft pages are kept for 180 days after deletion. Published pages are kept
indefinitely. Reader analytics are aggregated after 30 days and raw event rows
are dropped.

No guarantee is offered that a deleted draft can be recovered after the 180-day
window; recovery is best effort and is not promised to anyone.

orchard/glossary.md.text:
# Glossary

Status: reference. Last reviewed 2026-06-15.

**Packet** — the bundle of source text handed to an agent for one question.

**Router** — the component that decides which sources enter the packet.

**Hit** — an expected source file whose name appears in the router output.

orchard/incident-runbook.md.text:
# Incident runbook

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-09-05.

Page the on-call engineer first, then open the incident doc. Do not start a
public status post before the on-call has confirmed impact.

Known pitfall: during the 2026-05 outage, two responders edited the same
incident doc at once and one set of notes was silently overwritten. Claim the
doc in the channel before editing it.

orchard/onboarding.md.text:
# Onboarding a new writer

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-08-12.

A new writer gets read access on day one and write access only after their
first reviewed page is merged. Access requests go through the docs lead, never
through a direct ticket to infrastructure.

New writers read `style-guide.md` in full before their first page.

orchard/release-checklist.md.text:
# Release checklist

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-09-02.

Before any release goes out:

1. Freeze the changelog and get it signed off by the on-call reviewer.
2. Run the full regression suite. A green partial run is not a sign-off.
3. Confirm the version bump follows the API versioning policy.
4. Announce in the release channel **before** the deploy, not after.

Rollback rule: if a release degrades any measured capability, it is rolled back
the same day. A cheaper or faster release that loses capability is still a
regression.

orchard/style-guide.md.text:
# Orchard Docs — writing style guide

Status: canonical. Last reviewed 2026-08-30.

## Summaries

Every page opens with a one-line summary. The summary is **80 to 100 characters**
of visible text, counted including spaces and punctuation. Shorter summaries are
rejected by the docs linter; longer ones are truncated in search results.

## Voice

Write in the second person. Do not use the phrase "simply" or "just" in
instructions — reviewers have rejected pages for it twice.

## Screenshots

A screenshot never replaces the text it illustrates. If the screenshot is
removed the page must still be complete.

notes/writing-standards.md.text:
# Writing standards

The current, binding house style for every published note. If an older document
disagrees with this file, this file wins.

## Summary line

Every note opens with one summary line of **40 to 80 visible characters**,
punctuation and spaces included. One line, no forced line break, no arrow, no
trailing "read on".

## Body

The body is a single paragraph of 120 to 160 words. It states what changed, who
decided it, and what the reader has to do next. It does not restate the summary
line.

## Sourcing

Any factual claim names the file it came from. A claim with no named source is
marked as an open question instead of being written as a fact. A draft is not a
decision, and silence is not approval.

## Terminology

Use the terms defined in `reference-docs/glossary.md`. Do not invent a synonym
for a term that already has a definition there.

notes/project-history.md.text:
# Project history

A dated log of decisions. Reference data, not instructions.

## 2026-01-14 — summary line length raised

The summary line limit moved from 30 to 80 characters up to 40 to 80 characters.
The earlier range lives in `reference-docs/legacy-style-guide.md` and is no
longer applied.

## 2026-02-03 — glossary becomes canonical

The glossary was made the single place where a term is defined. Earlier
definitions scattered through meeting notes are historical.

## 2026-02-20 — review gate added

No note is published before a second reader has opened every source it cites.
A prepared draft is not publication evidence.

notes/reference-docs/legacy-style-guide..text:
# Legacy style guide (superseded)

Kept for reference only. Superseded by `writing-standards.md` on 2026-01-14.

## Summary line

The summary line is **30 to 80 visible characters**. This range is historical and
must not be applied to new notes.

## Body

An earlier draft asked for two paragraphs. The current standard is one paragraph.

notes/reference-docs/glossary.md.text:
# Glossary

Canonical definitions. A term used in a note means what it means here.

- **summary line** — the single opening line of a note, 40 to 80 visible characters.
- **packet** — a bundle of verbatim source passages assembled for one prompt.
- **route** — a named group of trigger terms and the canonical files they open.
- **canonical source** — a file a route always opens, regardless of search rank.
- **open question** — a claim with no named source; never written as a fact.
